keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «실패를 똑똑하지 않다는 증거로 보는 생각(잘못된 생각)» 과 «실수는 더 나아지는 데 꼭 필요하다(주장)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the common belief (failure proves you are not smart) and the claim (mistakes are a necessary part of getting better). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why do some students avoid challenges?
qs.qko: 왜 어떤 학생들은 어려운 일을 피할까요?
opts: because trying something hard risks another failure
because challenges are boring to them
because teachers do not allow them
evs: They ask what went wrong and how they could approach the problem differently next time.
This belief can make them avoid challenges, because trying something hard risks another failure.
Of course, effort alone is not enough; learners also need feedback and new methods.
Over time, this willingness leads to deeper and longer-lasting learning.
why: 어려운 일에 도전하면 또 실패할 위험이 있다고 믿기 때문이라고 했어요.
The text says trying something hard risks another failure, so they avoid it.

qs.q: In the text, what does "a final judgment" mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 «a final judgment(최종 판정)» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: a decision that proves your ability is fixed
a test given at the end of the year
a piece of advice about a new strategy
evs: Many students see failure as proof that they are not smart enough.
In fact, struggling with a difficult problem often helps people remember the solution better later.
Psychologist Carol Dweck describes two ways of thinking about ability.
Over time, this willingness leads to deeper and longer-lasting learning.
why: 많은 학생이 실패를 «똑똑하지 않다는 증거» 로 본다고 했어요. 최종 판정은 바로 이런 생각, 즉 내 능력이 정해져 있다는 결론이에요.
Many students see failure as proof that they are not smart enough. A final judgment is that kind of fixed conclusion about ability.

qs.q: What happens over time when people treat failure as a step in the process?
qs.qko: 실패를 과정의 한 단계로 여기면 시간이 지나 어떤 일이 생기나요?
opts: They learn more deeply and remember longer.
They need less feedback from teachers.
They start to avoid hard problems.
evs: Still, treating failure as a step in the process makes people more willing to take on challenges.
However, research on learning suggests that mistakes are a necessary part of getting better.
Over time, this willingness leads to deeper and longer-lasting learning.
When they get a low test score, they may decide that they are simply bad at math or science.
why: 실패를 과정으로 보면 도전에 더 적극적이 되고, 그 적극성이 시간이 지나 더 깊고 오래가는 배움으로 이어져요.
Treating failure as a step makes people more willing to take on challenges, and over time this leads to deeper, longer-lasting learning.

write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «조건 + 그때 할 수 있는 일» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write a condition and what we can do then.
write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «If» 뒤에는 «누가 + 무엇을 하면» 을, «we can» 뒤에는 동사원형을 넣어 보세요. (예: If we sleep early, we can focus in class)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «If», write who + what; after «we can», start with a base verb. (e.g. If we sleep early, we can focus in class)
